algorithms.name: Bivariate Choropleth Map
algorithms.help:
Creates a 2D Bivariate Choropleth thematic map classifying two numeric fields simultaneously into an NxN colour matrix (2x2, 3x3, or 4x4).

Supports 5 curated cartographic palette presets (Stevens Pink-Cyan, Teal-Brown, Blue-Orange, Purple-Green, Night Neon) or custom corner colours.

Outputs an automatically styled layer with high-quality translucent outlines and human-readable class descriptions (e.g. Low-Low, High-High).

params.name: CLASSES
params.description: Number of classes per axis (N x N)

params.name: COLOR_LL
params.description: Bottom-Left colour (Low X, Low Y) [if Custom]

params.name: COLOR_LH
params.description: Top-Left colour (Low X, High Y) [if Custom]

params.name: COLOR_HL
params.description: Bottom-Right colour (High X, Low Y) [if Custom]

params.name: COLOR_HH
params.description: Top-Right colour (High X, High Y) [if Custom]

algorithms.name: Export Bivariate 2D Legend Matrix
algorithms.help:
Generate a standalone vector polygon layer and HTML preview of an NxN bivariate colour legend matrix (2x2, 3x3, or 4x4).

• Supports standard square grid or 45-degree diamond cartographic layout.
• Built-in curated palettes (Stevens Pink-Cyan, Teal-Brown, Blue-Orange, Purple-Green, Night Neon) or custom corner colours.
• Each cell carries col, row, class code, label, and hex colour code.
• Automatically styled with categorized renderer and crisp white borders.

params.name: CLASSES
params.description: Number of classes per axis (N x N)

params.name: COLOR_LL
params.description: Bottom-Left colour (Low X, Low Y) [if Custom]

params.name: COLOR_LH
params.description: Top-Left colour (Low X, High Y) [if Custom]

params.name: COLOR_HL
params.description: Bottom-Right colour (High X, Low Y) [if Custom]

params.name: COLOR_HH
params.description: Top-Right colour (High X, High Y) [if Custom]

algorithms.name: Apply 2.5D Building Style
algorithms.help: Apply a polished native QGIS 2.5D renderer to a loaded polygon layer. The selected field can be a real height or a floor-count field. CartoLab controls the roof colour, wall colour, shadow, viewing angle, optional height clamp, optional stepped extrusion, and sample-QML-style per-floor colour bands.

params.name: HEIGHT_MODE
options: Height field is already in metres/map units
Floor count field (floors x floor height)

params.name: FLOOR_HEIGHT
params.description: Floor height, used only when height source is floor count

params.name: FLOOR_PALETTE
params.description: Floor colour palette, used by per-floor bands

params.name: MAX_FLOORS
params.description: Maximum floor bands, 0 scans the layer automatically

params.name: MAX_HEIGHT
params.description: Maximum rendered height, 0 for no clamp

algorithms.name: Continuous-Area Cartogram (Diffusion)
algorithms.help:
Distort polygon areas to be proportional to a numeric field using the diffusion method (Gastner & Newman).

The algorithm iteratively displaces polygon boundaries until each region's area represents its field value. A zero-width buffer is applied to fix topology issues on exit.

• Color ramp: Automatically styles the resulting distorted polygons.
Requires at least 2 valid polygon features.

algorithms.name: Dorling Circle Cartogram
algorithms.help:
Replace every areal unit with a circle whose area is proportional to a value, then move the circles apart until none overlap (Dorling 1996).

Unlike a continuous cartogram, shapes are not deformed: each unit is an honest, directly comparable circle, and small units with large values stay visible.

• Size factor: the circles' total area as a share of the input layer's area. Lower values give more space between circles and smaller displacements.
• Attraction: how strongly circles are pulled back toward their home position while they separate (fades to zero, so the result never overlaps).
• Gap: extra spacing between circles, in layer units.
• Units with a missing, zero or negative value are omitted.

Output fields: every input field plus dor_value, dor_radius and dor_shift (distance moved from the unit's interior point). Use a projected CRS: circles are built in layer units.

params.name: SIZE_FACTOR
params.description: Size factor (total circle area / layer area)

outputs.name: RESIDUAL
outputs.description: Residual overlap (fraction of mean radius, <= 0 = none)

algorithms.name: Dot-Density Map
algorithms.help:
Scatter dots inside each polygon, one dot per N units of a count field, so density reads as visual texture rather than colour.

Placement is seeded (re-runs are identical) and hole-aware. Each dot inherits the source polygon's attributes, so you can colour dots by category for a multi-group dot map.

• Value per dot: Choose so the busiest polygon shows a few hundred dots.
• Marker size & color: Configured directly in millimeters and RGBA.

algorithms.name: Origin-Destination Flow Map
algorithms.help:
Draw desire lines between zones from an origin-destination table (commuting, migration, trade, trips).

• Zones: any layer with an id field; polygons are represented by a point guaranteed to lie inside them.
• Flows: any table or layer with origin id, destination id and volume fields — a CSV without geometry works. Repeated pairs are summed; ids match as text, so 7, 7.0 and "7" are the same zone.
• Curved flows bend to the right of travel, so A→B and B→A become two separate arcs. Curvature 0 draws straight lines. Merge the directions to map total two-way volume instead.
• Line width is linear in volume; colour classes are quantiles. Large flows are drawn underneath small ones so nothing is hidden.
• Filter with a minimum volume and/or keep only the top N flows.

Output fields: flow_o, flow_d, flow_vol, flow_rank (1 = largest), flow_share (% of mapped volume), flow_width (mm), flow_len (map units).

params.name: TOP_N
params.description: Keep only the N largest flows (0 = all)

params.name: END_GAP
params.description: Gap at each end (% of flow length)

algorithms.name: Advanced Classification (GIC / Head-Tail / Jenks / StdDev / BoxPlot / Max / Pretty)
algorithms.help:
Classify a numeric field using advanced cartographic algorithms.

• Adaptive GIC: Optimal for skewed continuous and geometric growth data.
• Head/Tail Breaks: Optimal for heavy-tailed / power-law spatial distributions.
• Fisher-Jenks: Natural breaks minimising within-class variance.
• Standard Deviation: Symmetrical interval breaks centered at the sample mean.
• Box Plot / Tukey: Outlier-resistant quartile and fence boundaries.
• Maximum Breaks: Splits data at the largest natural distribution gaps.
• Pretty Breaks: Heckbert algorithm for clean rounded interval boundaries.

Output carries 'gic_class' (0-based integer index) and 'gic_label' fields, and is styled automatically with the chosen color ramp.

algorithms.name: Graticule / Reference Grid
algorithms.help:
Generate a line layer of meridians and parallels across an extent, on 'nice' round coordinate intervals. Each line carries its orientation, constant coordinate and a formatted label (label it with the 'label' field).

• Auto-picks nice rounded step intervals (~8 lines across extent) if left at 0.
• Direct styling control: Solid, Dashed, Dotted, or Dash-Dot with custom color and line width.
The output uses the extent's CRS — set the extent in the CRS you want the grid drawn in.

algorithms.name: Hexbin Aggregation
algorithms.help:
Aggregate a point layer into a pointy-top hexagonal grid. Only hexagons that actually contain points are emitted, so dense scatter plots become a clean, overplot-free density surface.

• Statistic: Point count, sum of weight, or mean of weight.
• Cell size: Hexagon radius in layer's map units.
• Color Palette & Classifier: Direct styling with Quantile, Equal Interval, Jenks, or Pretty breaks.
Output carries hex_count, hex_sum, hex_mean and is graduated automatically.

algorithms.name: Visual-Center Label Points
algorithms.help:
Compute each polygon's pole of inaccessibility (polylabel) — the interior point furthest from any edge. Unlike a centroid, it always falls inside the polygon, even for C-shaped or doughnut features, so labels never spill outside the shape.

For multipart features the largest part is used.
• 'lbl_dist': Inscribed-circle radius in map units (available label room proxy).
• 'lbl_angle': Principal inertia orientation angle in degrees [-90..+90] for rotating labels along elongated shapes.

Precision 0 = auto (scaled from each polygon's size).

algorithms.name: Choropleth Normalization & Rates
algorithms.help:
Turn a raw field into a map-ready value before choropleth classification. Mapping a raw count as colour is the classic error (it just redraws population); normalise first.

  - Rate: numerator / denominator x scale (e.g. cases per 100k)
  - Location Quotient (LQ): specialisation index relative to benchmark base
  - Z-score / Robust z (median-MAD) / Robust IQR (median-IQR): standardise for comparison
  - Min-max / Winsorized min-max: rescale to 0-1 with optional outlier clamping
  - Percentile / Decile rank / Tukey Hinge: distribution position and box-plot binning
  - Log / Sigmoid / Power (Box-Cox): tame heavy right tails and stabilize variance

Writes 'norm_value' and 'norm_method' fields, and graduates the output layer automatically.

params.name: METHOD
options: Tukey Hinge Rank (1-6 Box Plot class)

params.name: CLASSES
params.description: Number of classes for graduated style

algorithms.name: Proportional Symbols (Flannery)
algorithms.help:
Convert any vector layer to point symbols sized proportionally to a numeric field, using Flannery perceptual compensation by default.

Readers systematically under-estimate circle area; Flannery scaling (exponent ~0.57) compensates so visual perception matches true data ratios.

• Shapes: Circle, Square, Diamond, Triangle, Star.
• Colors: Configurable fill and outline colors with RGBA transparency.
Outputs point geometries at centroids with 'psym_value' and 'psym_size' (symbol size in mm) fields, styled automatically with a data-defined renderer.

algorithms.name: Quick Style (auto choropleth / categories)
algorithms.help:
Style an existing vector layer in place without creating a copy.

Pick a field and a palette name: numeric fields become a graduated choropleth with ColorBrewer / colour-blind-safe palettes; string fields become a categorized map.

In 'Auto' mode the layer field type decides whether graduated or categorized is applied.

Monochrome print-safe: polygon layers get black-and-white hatch and dot patterns instead of colours, so the map survives greyscale printing and photocopies. Graduated classes darken strictly with the value (up to 10 classes); categories differ by texture and orientation (up to 16 before patterns repeat).

algorithms.name: Ridge Map (Joy Division Style)
algorithms.help:
Generate a ridge-line (joy division style) vector layer from a single-band raster. The raster values deform scanlines vertically, producing overlapping wave profiles.

• Vertical exaggeration & Line spacing: Control wave crest height and frequency.
• Line color & width: Configured directly for publication rendering.
Best raster inputs: DEM elevation, population density surfaces, LST, urban heat index.

algorithms.name: Value-by-Alpha (VbA) Map
algorithms.help:
Encode uncertainty/reliability as opacity (alpha channel).

• Primary variable drives color gradient.
• Secondary reliability variable controls opacity (High reliability = opaque, Low = transparent).
• Color Palette & Classes: Direct sequential ramp selection.
Adds 'vba_alpha' (0-255) and 'vba_alpha_pct' (0-100) fields and sets up data-defined opacity renderer.
